citations.where: lesson radioactivity-is-natural: The discovery of radioactivity in a natural mineral.
citations.quote: On enveloppe une plaque photographique Lumière, au gélatino-bromure, avec deux feuilles de papier noir très épais
citations.comment: Quote transcribed by eye from the scanned page 421 (no text layer). The 24 Feb 1896 note reports that a uranium potassium double sulfate (crystals he possessed), exposed to the Sun, blackens a wrapped plate. It does not claim a new natural radioactivity, and the material is a crystalline salt, not described as a mineral. It is the first of Becquerel's notes, not the discovery of radioactivity as such.

citations.where: blog "the banana on your counter" (Becquerel 1896: uranium mineral on a wrapped plate, plate fogged even with no sunlight)
citations.comment: The cited note (pp. 420-421) has the salt exposed to the Sun for several hours; the 'no sunlight' result is NOT in it. It is in the next note, 2 March 1896, 'Sur les radiations invisibles émises par les corps phosphorescents', Comptes rendus 122 pp. 501-503 (https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/dossiers/Becquerel/Becquerel_pdf/CR1896_p501.pdf, fetched and read as page images), p. 502: 'mais à l'abri des radiations incidentes et maintenues à l'obscurité produisent encore les mêmes impressions photographiques.' That note supports the claim; it also uses the same potassium uranyl sulfate salt, so 'uranium mineral' is a simplification. The 'natural mineral, long before nuclear technology' framing is the app's own and is not in either note.

problems: Row cites the 24 Feb note, but the 'plate fogged with no sunlight' claim in the blog comes from the 2 March 1896 note (pp. 501-503).
Becquerel used a crystalline uranium potassium sulfate salt, not a natural mineral; 'uranium mineral' overstates the source.
Row title omits accents ('emises'); the printed title is 'émises'.
suggestedFix: Add the 2 March 1896 note (Sur les radiations invisibles émises par les corps phosphorescents, C. R. 122, 501-503) as a second source for the 'no sunlight' sentence, and word the lesson as 'a uranium salt' or 'a uranium compound' rather than 'natural mineral'. Set URL to the Académie PDF for the 24 Feb note.
